answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each identity to maintain a private computational orchard whose growth is driven by a unique zephyr of random challenges that embed an onyx-hard personal seed. Only agents presenting a recent verifiable branch from their orchard may enter the shared resource pool. Creating many fake agents forces an attacker to run independent orchards, each consuming distinct compute and storage that cannot be cheaply cloned without failing consistency checks against the zephyr updates.
